name: Ghugni
instructions: 1. Soak dried yellow peas overnight and pressure cook them with salt and turmeric until tender.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan, temper with bay leaf and cumin seeds.
3. Sauté onions, ginger-garlic paste, and tomatoes until soft.
4. Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, and red chili powders with a splash of water to form a masala paste.
5. Add cubed potatoes and fry until browned.
6. Mix in the boiled peas, adjust water consistency, and simmer for 10 minutes.
7. Finish by adding garam masala, tamarind pulp, and fresh coriander, and serve topped with chopped onions and roasted cumin powder.
description: Ghugni is a quintessential Bengali street food staple. It is a hearty, comfort-food curry made from dried yellow peas, typically served in small bowls or 'shoras' and topped with fresh garnishes, representing the vibrant and soulful snack culture of Kolkata.
